discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the founding of neutrino astronomy with a cubic-kilometre ice detector
motivation: IceCube turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a telescope and in 2013 discovered a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, opening a new window on the universe. It then identified the first sources: the flaring blazar TXS 0506+056 (2018, with multi-messenger follow-up), the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 (2022), and neutrino emission from the Galactic plane (2023). These results establish neutrinos as astronomical messengers that reveal hadronic cosmic accelerators hidden to photons. Francis Halzen conceived and led IceCube from the AMANDA prototype to discovery. Albrecht Karle shaped the detector concept, its construction and the high-energy analyses that produced the discovery. Christian Spiering pioneered deep-water and ice neutrino telescopes (Baikal, AMANDA) and brought the European community into IceCube. Their bold instrument and patient data-taking created a new field of astronomy.
